record.original_question: Is any of the three classical properties S_fin(Ω, Ω), S_1(Γ, Ω), or S_fin(Γ, Ω) consistently closed under finite unions?

evidence.quote: Problem 8.4 ([60]). Is any of the classes Sfin(Ω, Ω), S1(Γ, Ω), and Sfin(Γ, Ω) consistently closed under taking finite unions?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be an infinite topological space (typically a set of real numbers or a Tychonoff space). An open cover U of X is called an ω-cover if X itself is not a member of U and for every finite subset F ⊆ X there exists U ∈ U with F ⊆ U. An open cover U of X is called a γ-cover if U is infinite and for every x ∈ X the set {U ∈ U : x ∉ U} is finite. Denote by Ω the family of open ω-covers of X and by Γ the family of open γ-covers of X.

For collections A and B of covers, define the following selection principles:
• S_1(A, B): For every sequence (U_n)_{n∈ℕ} of elements of A there exist U_n ∈ U_n such that {U_n : n ∈ ℕ} ∈ B.
• S_fin(A, B): For every sequence (U_n)_{n∈ℕ} of elements of A there exist finite sets F_n ⊆ U_n such that ⋃_{n∈ℕ} F_n ∈ B.

A class C of topological spaces is said to be closed under finite unions if whenever X, Y ∈ C the topological sum (equivalently, the union, when X and Y are subspaces of a common space) X ∪ Y also belongs to C.

Question: Is it consistent with the axioms of ZFC that at least one of the three classes
  S_fin(Ω, Ω),   S_1(Γ, Ω),   S_fin(Γ, Ω)
(viewed as classes of spaces satisfying the corresponding selection principle) is closed under finite unions?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is listed as an open problem in surveys of selection principles. Subsequent literature (e.g., Tsaban's surveys and follow-up papers on point-cofinite covers, Laver model results) continues to reference it as open; no published resolution showing consistent closure under finite unions of any of S_fin(Ω,Ω), S_1(Γ,Ω), or S_fin(Γ,Ω) was found.
